pms.thesis: Take profit on half the existing 2027 CORRA H/M/U/Z receive while preserving a 250m residual. The November 2 frozen contract mids average 3.16%, down from the 3.40% entry; roughly 62bp of 2027 tightening remains priced above 2.54% CORRA. September underlying Canadian inflation near 1.85% and unemployment near 6.5% still challenge a full hiking cycle, but the late-October BoC hike and Brent around 105 weaken the one-way receive thesis.

positions.thesis: AUDNZD at 1.2456 is a five-year extreme while NZDUSD still sits in the cheap tail at 0.5627. That cross has stretched far beyond a 30-basis-point Australia versus New Zealand 10-year gap, and it is the only concentrated, asymmetric swing on a firm tape. Short the cross as a real swing; oil remaining bid is the accepted tax, not a reason to stay flat. CORRA March stays closed: 2.55 cash versus 2.925 is the same leftover path already booked into the event-implied print, not a new dislocation…

pms.thesis: AUD/NZD is still a crowded high-percentile cross after a modest overnight fade, with kiwi washed out on the dollar and no fresh Australian policy shock to justify the spread. The swing still has room toward 1.20-1.22 on a multi-week horizon; a small oil dip does not reverse Australia's terms-of-trade premium enough to close that gap. Cash-versus-March leftovers in SOFR, CORRA, and TONA are already in the tape and do not clear a new rates book versus sitting in the existing cross. Being behind on the scoreboard is not a reason to layer correlated receive risk or to cut a working short that has not reached the realization zone.

positions.thesis: That is the first 2027 three-month contract that prices a Canadian hiking cycle (+84bp vs CORRA cash 2.29) after 1m CORRA still only reaches 2.58 by Dec-2026 and Dec-26 3m CRAZ26 is 2.775. August labor (-42k, wages +2.0%) and CPI-trim/median 1.9/2.0 do not support delivering that 2027 path. Side long is duration-long in implied-rate space (profits if the 3.13 implied falls toward the still-alive near-term path).

positions.thesis: March Canada still prices 37.5 basis points of hike versus 2.55 cash, so the 450 million receive stays the core and does not need harvest. The New Zealand versus US 10-year residual has fully retraced from about 23 basis points cheap to zero, and I am flattening it rather than nursing a name I cannot add. AUDNZD at 1.2456 is a 99.6 five-year extreme with kiwi already at a 3.5 five-year cheap print after the late-October New Zealand surprise; a 20 million short of the cross is a tactical FX…

pms.thesis: Canada March still embeds about 43 basis points of unused tightening versus cash, and the overnight oil dip is a mild growth-impulse fade, not a reason to pay the leftover. AUDNZD remains crowded near the 94th percentile of the past year, so the tactical short still has a mean-reversion path as long as a Hormuz shock does not drive kiwi through its lows and the cross to new highs. I am not adding U.S. leftover, dollar-yen, or oil-Canada FX: those either duplicate beta already in the book or sit at extended levels that do not improve the adverse path.

pms.thesis: AUDNZD is still near the top of its one-year range at 1.2417 after drifting from 1.2456, so the existing short retains a swing path if the cross leaves that extreme toward the recent distribution. Fresh tickets in NZDUSD, AUDCAD, USDJPY, or March leftovers would expand risk into a mid-range oil cross, a stretched yen, or a two-way 41 to 44 basis-point cash-versus-March strip that still sits against Brent near 103.60. Official overnight on shocked capital is the hurdle those new ideas fail; the working ten-million cross does not need to be enlarged.
